title: Euripidis Hecuba, Orestes, Phoenissae (Barocci 120)
shelf_note: A Byzantine minuscule manuscript of Euripides with interlinear glosses and marginal scholia. That matches a Barocci Euripides of the early 14th century. The page is Orestes 954–981. No collection is recorded, so there is no shelf to contradict.
structure_note: The structure counts disagree with each other: pages_translated is 0 in the structure counts but 217 in the field (E2). This manuscript has no printed pagination, and this leaf has no number on it at all, only a '+' at the head. So the 120 'printed numbers', with 15 backsteps and 15 repeats, are almost certainly model-assigned or misread values, not a real break in page order.

pages.layout: single column of verse in a minuscule hand, with dense interlinear glosses and scholia in the left margin. There are two red marginal signs (a χρ monogram and 'ΝΧ'), a '+' at the head, and an edge of the facing leaf at the right (correctly ignored).

book_verdict: On this page the OCR misreads most of the main verse (Orestes 954–981) and invents lines: a Zeus invocation, a 'Laconian frenzy'. It also drops two lines into gloss tags, and the translation renders all of it as fluent English. The closing notes quote the standard text correctly. They are the only reliable guide on the page, and most of the interlinear glosses cannot be verified or are wrong.
